title: Air India Doubles Down on Australia With Premium Upgrades and Daily Flights
excerpt: The Tata-owned carrier is deploying Boeing 777-300ERs with First Class on Delhi-Melbourne from July and ramping to daily service by September, as India-Australia air travel demand hits record highs.
body:
• Air India has replaced its Boeing 787-8 with an upgraded 777-300ER on Delhi-Melbourne, adding First Class suites and onboard Wi-Fi from July 1, 2026.
  • The airline will increase Delhi-Melbourne from four weekly flights to daily service starting September 1, marking a major capacity expansion on the route.
  • Air India is evaluating new nonstop services to Adelaide or Brisbane, with potential flights from Mumbai and Bengaluru as it aims to dominate the India-Australia corridor.

Air India has upgraded its Delhi-Melbourne service with a larger Boeing 777-300ER aircraft featuring First Class, expanded Business Class seating, and onboard Wi-Fi — the latest move in an aggressive push into Australia that has seen the carrier's passenger numbers on the route surge by double digits year over year.

The aircraft swap, effective July 1, brings eight First Class suites, 40 fully flat Business Class seats, and 280 Economy seats to the route, according to the airline. That is a significant step up from the Boeing 787-8 previously operating the service, which carried 28 Business seats and 241 Economy seats with no First Class cabin, Travelobiz reported.

From Four Flights a Week to Daily

Air India currently operates four nonstop flights per week between Delhi and Melbourne. From September 1, 2026, the airline plans to increase frequency to daily service, restoring capacity that was temporarily trimmed during the June-August period when airspace restrictions and record jet fuel prices — which hit $162.89 per barrel in May 2026 — forced cuts across the international network, according to The Hindu BusinessLine.

The airline maintained eight weekly flights to Australia even during the summer reductions, according to TTR Weekly, while suspending or cutting service on six other international routes including Delhi-Chicago and Mumbai-New York.

A Market That Keeps Growing

The expansion reflects a broader surge in India-Australia air travel. Air India carried approximately 220,000 roundtrip passengers on its Australia flights in the first nine months of 2022, a 44% increase over the same period in 2019, according to booking data analyzed by Simple Flying. By the year ending February 2024, the carrier had provided 391,168 seats on 1,528 flights and carried 338,179 passengers at an 86% load factor — representing an 82% increase in flights and capacity compared to pre-pandemic levels, aviation analytics firm Analytic Flying reported.

Air India is now the dominant carrier on the India-Australia corridor, accounting for 66% of direct capacity and 65% of passengers, ahead of Qantas, according to the same analysis.

"Air India's non-stop services will increasingly cater to the diverse needs of residents, businesspeople, students, and tourists within the Indian-Australian community."

— Campbell Wilson, CEO & MD, Air India

Adelaide or Brisbane Could Be Next

The carrier is not stopping at Melbourne and Sydney. Air India is evaluating new nonstop flights to either Adelaide or Brisbane in 2026, sources told The Hindu BusinessLine in February. The proposed services would be operated using refurbished Boeing 787 aircraft, though timelines depend on when those jets return from Air India's ongoing cabin retrofit program.

Sources indicated the new Australian services could be launched from Mumbai or Bengaluru rather than Delhi, in line with the airline's strategy to distribute long-haul operations across multiple metro hubs. Air India currently operates daily Delhi-Sydney flights and launched a Mumbai-Melbourne service in December 2023, the first nonstop link between Australia and India's financial capital.

What It Means for the Indian Diaspora

Australia is home to nearly one million people of Indian origin, making it one of the largest Indian diaspora communities outside South Asia. Tourism Australia has projected one million annual arrivals from India by 2030, which would make India its third-largest source market. Indian visitors already account for 5.3% of all visitor arrivals in Australia, up from 3.2% a decade ago, according to Analytic Flying data.

For Indian-Americans and NRIs who frequently travel between the U.S., India, and Australia — for family visits, business, or education — the expanded service through Delhi offers convenient one-stop connections. Delhi serves as Air India's primary hub for onward connections to London, Frankfurt, Paris, Rome, Milan, and Zurich, meaning the Australia upgrades effectively improve connectivity across Air India's entire long-haul network.

Premium Competition Heats Up

The Boeing 777-300ER deployment also signals intensifying competition on premium India-Australia travel. Eligible First and Business Class passengers departing Delhi will have access to Air India's new Maharaja Lounge at Indira Gandhi International Airport, featuring upgraded dining and pre-flight facilities.

The airline's record-breaking order of 470 new aircraft — with deliveries arriving roughly every six days — underpins the expansion. Air India currently operates six upgraded Boeing 777s, six Airbus A350s, and seven Boeing 787-9s, with five more widebody aircraft expected in 2026, though most incoming jets are earmarked for North American and European routes.

For travelers from cities like Mumbai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Chennai, and Kolkata, Delhi remains the primary gateway to Australia. The upgraded aircraft and daily frequency mean passengers connecting through the capital can now access a premium long-haul product without relying on Gulf or Southeast Asian carriers — a shift Air India CEO Campbell Wilson has framed as filling "the void left by foreign carriers with non-stop flights and Indian hospitality."
